extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Single printed SoA table, Section 1.3 of protocol J2A-MC-GZGI(a), document pages 13-18 (printed footers read 12-17, one lower; PAGEMAP.md is authoritative). Header band (Study Period / Screening-Lead-In / Visit Number / Week Relative to Randomization / Allowable Interval Tolerance / Fasting Visit) reprints at the top of every page and was de-duplicated to six schedule_property rows. Column model: 21 physical columns, L=1 label column, data columns 2-21 (Visits 1-18, ET, 801). Marks were re-derived mechanically from the pdftotext/PyMuPDF text-layer bboxes binned to the 21 rule-line column bands, and diffed against a visual read of 150 dpi renders. Full-width instruction text blocks printed beneath an activity's mark row were captured as footnote annotations (prompt Section 4: instruction-overflow rows are not activities), each with a synthesised marker n1-n14. The abbreviations block under the table yielded zero annotations: no term in it is printed as a marker on a grid cell, header cell or activity label (prompt Section 6).

table_metadata.table_purpose: Primary schedule of activities for Study J2A-MC-GZGI(a): Screening/Lead-in (Study Period I), Treatment Period Visits 3-18 plus early termination (Study Period II), and the Safety Follow-Up visit 801 (Study Period III).
table_metadata.notes: Classified main_soa: rows are procedures performed on participants and this is the protocol's only, primary anchor grid. The page breaks at document pages 14-18 fall inside one printed table with a reprinted header band and no separate table number or caption, so per the table-type definitions this is ONE table spanning pages 13-18, not a chain of 'continuation' tables. Column geometry read from the vector rule lines: 22 vertical rules -> 21 columns; column 1 is the activity-label column (L=1) and data columns run 2-21. The 'Pharmacokinetic (PK) sample' label cell is vertically merged over two grid rows whose sub-labels 'Predose' and 'Postdose' are printed in the Screening column (column 2); those two cells are row labels, not schedule marks, so no activity_schedule entry was emitted at column 2 for rows 67-68 and the sub-label was folded into activity_name.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Top header band naming the three major study periods: 'Study Period I Screening/Lead-in' merged over the Screening and Lead-In columns, 'Study Period II Treatment Period' merged over Visits 3-18, an unlabelled cell over the ET column, and 'Study Period III Safety Follow-Up' over Visit 801. Values are major study phases, so property_type=epoch.

Second header band. Its label cell (column 1) is empty; the row prints 'Screening' over the Visit 1 column and 'Lead-In' over the Visit 2 column, sub-dividing Study Period I. Sub-phase labels, so property_type=period. Name synthesised from the row's own cell values.

Visit identifiers for each schedule column: 1-18 for the scheduled visits, 'ET' for the early-termination visit and '801' for the safety follow-up visit. Named visit identifiers, so property_type=visit.
Study week of each visit relative to randomization (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 4 ... 36), '-' for the ET column and '2 Wks Post End of TXP' for Visit 801. Week numbers, so property_type=week.
Permitted visit window in days for each column ('-' where no window applies, '±3' elsewhere). Visit windows, so property_type=window.

Marks with 'X' which visits are fasting visits (every column except the Lead-In visit). This is an attribute/type of the visit rather than a timing concept, so property_type=modality. hierarchical_level is null: removing the row leaves every column still distinguishable by Visit Number.

annotations.annotation_text: The Schedule of Activities described below should be followed for all participants enrolled in Study GZGI. However, for those participants whose participation in this study is affected by exceptional circumstances, such as pandemics or natural disasters, please refer to Section 10.11 (Appendix 11) for additional guidance.
For early terminations that occur before the last visit in treatment period, see the activities listed for ET in this table. Shaded columns represent the dose escalation period Weeks 0-16.

Vital signs include pulse rate, blood pressure, and temperature. Vital sign measurements should be collected after participant has been sitting for at least 5 minutes and before obtaining an ECG tracing and before collection of blood samples for laboratory testing (see Section 10.7).
As indicated based on participant status and standard of care. May be performed by qualified personnel per local regulations.

Single central ECGs will be performed at screening and early termination. Central ECGs should be collected in triplicate at all other visits. ECG should be collected prior to collection of blood samples, including PK samples. ECG measurements should be obtained per the instructions in Section 8.2.3.
Participants should return the ABPM device at the conclusion of the 24- to 27-hour monitoring period.

At the time participant visit data are uploaded by the site, the ABPM Data Validity Report will be generated and should be reviewed to ensure ≥70% of readings are valid. If <70% of readings are valid, the 24-hour monitoring session should be repeated within the visit window.
May be performed more frequently based on usual site practices and participant needs.
May be performed based on participant needs.
The date and time of all dose administrations will be recorded in the log by the participant the day prior to a study visit, but may be recorded more frequently depending on site usual practice.
The Participant Survey should be administered at early termination if it occurs before 26 weeks.

Collect serum estradiol, FSH, and LH in women whose menopausal status needs to be determined. For participants known to be either premenopausal or postmenopausal, these tests do not need to be collected.

PK predose sample should be collected predose (~up to 1 hour predose). PK postdose sample time windows: 3-6 hours postdose (Week 4); 6-12 hours postdose (Week 8), 1-3 hours postdose (Week 16), 3-6 hours postdose (Week 26). Participants may need to return to clinical site for additional PK-specific visits to provide postdose PK samples.

One bottle of capsules is to be dispensed at Visit 3 and at Visit 4. Two bottles of capsules are to be dispensed at Visits 5-9 (during the rest of the dose escalation period). The site pharmacy should clearly label which bottle to take first. At Visits 10-17, 4 bottles of capsules should be dispensed.
